name: What happens if my Jacuzzi project runs into hidden plumbing or drainage problems?

mainEntity.name: What should I do if excavation reveals old plumbing, poor drainage, or unexpected site damage during Jacuzzi construction?
mainEntity.text: What should I do if excavation reveals old plumbing, poor drainage, or unexpected site damage during Jacuzzi construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden site problems are common in remodeling and custom construction, especially in older Los Angeles neighborhoods. Once excavation starts, the crew may uncover broken pipes, poor drainage, soil issues, or old repairs that were never documented. The right response is to stop and reassess rather than push forward blindly. The contractor should explain what was found, what it means for the design, and whether the fix affects budget or timeline. In many cases, it is better to address the underlying issue immediately than build over it and risk future leaks or settlement. Homeowners should ask for photos and a written change order if the scope changes. Transparent communication matters here because hidden conditions can be legitimate, but they should always be documented. A well-managed project treats these discoveries as part of responsible construction, not as an excuse for vague costs.
acceptedAnswer.description: If hidden plumbing or drainage problems are found, the project should pause so the contractor can re-evaluate the scope, pricing, and design. Fixing the issue before closing up the work is far cheaper than covering it and dealing with failure later.
